scope: Repair actual legacy Jupiter build/dispatch retry and duplicated SDK signing paths; own managed local signing cancellation. Verification uses detached synthetic keys, fake HTTP/RPC and actual SDK/consumer code only. No operator signing, wallet/provider network call, live order or runtime launch is authorized.
user_objective: Preserve requested exact 0.1 SOL paper entries and existing uncapped extreme-runner protection; learning targets above 100/200 percent are not take-profit caps or guaranteed cash returns. Reliable execution is necessary but cannot make the strategy profitable by itself.
findings: The legacy Jupiter retry loop included signing/broadcast. A lost response after a possibly accepted submission could build and sign a different order.
The duplicate Jupiter signer used outdated SDK imports and message/legacy mutation assumptions; correcting the separate common signer did not repair this distinct caller.
Legacy signing/RPC blocked the shared event loop; managed signing used an unowned worker. Cancellation could abandon actual in-flight work.
The actual seller discarded checked QuoteResult identity before execution and conservatively could not distinguish a proven unsigned-build failure from a possibly submitted transaction.

implementation.build_snapshot: Detach and recheck quote raw data, original checked metadata, complete route contract, exact uint64 amounts, impact and slippage before HTTP. Freeze payload and validate strict retry/boolean/wallet inputs before each bounded unsigned request. A raw-dict compatibility call is sanity checked but does not independently prove the original caller request intent.
implementation.unsigned_retry: Only HTTP429, HTTP5xx, connection errors and timeout during unsigned construction retry, with at most max_retries+1 requests and retry bound0..5. Zero retries means one initial request. Close each response/session before backoff. Other HTTP, JSON/schema/base64/alias/size failures do not retry or invoke dispatch.
implementation.packet_transport: Check nonempty strict base64, consistent canonical/compatibility aliases, optional integer uint64 response metadata and supported legacy/v0 packet bound1232 bytes. Do not claim support for newer v1 transaction format or certify freshness, priority budget or unsigned instruction content.
implementation.dispatch_once: Remove the duplicate signer and invoke the existing common current-SDK sign_and_send once, outside the build retry loop, through run_owned_sync. Preserve original bytes/signature and inherited matching-acknowledgement endpoint relay rules. Ordinary errors after entering dispatch are SwapSubmissionUncertain, even if the callable raises SwapPreparationError; no rebuild/re-sign/order fallback is allowed.
implementation.preparation_fallback: SwapPreparationError proves this actual adapter has not entered its signing/send callable. Preserve actual checked QuoteResult in the seller and allow existing liquidity-gated canonical-mint GMGN fallback only at this proven pre-dispatch boundary. All post-dispatch errors remain uncertain; no financial fill is invented.
implementation.managed_ownership: Move the existing managed local signing callable onto the same owned worker mechanism. Repeated cancellation joins signing before propagating cancellation and cannot continue to execute POST afterward. Managed response/request/content/finality validation and protocol migration are explicitly separate incomplete work.
implementation.unchanged: No .env, operator key, active model, policy, order size, activation gate or upside ceiling is changed. All fixture package replacements use direct namespace assignment rather than invoking the operator's lazy signer import.
